2026-06963.headline: Stablecoin freeze power: a FinCEN/OFAC proposal would require issuers to be able to block, freeze and reject transactions
2026-06963.what_changed: A joint proposed rule (91 FR 18582; RIN 1506-AB73; docket FINCEN-2026-0100) would treat permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs) as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act and require AML and sanctions-compliance programs. Comments closed in June 2026, and no final rule was found.
2026-06963.summary: Under the GENIUS Act (P.L. 119-27), an issuer may issue payment stablecoins only if it can technically comply with lawful orders to seize, freeze, burn or block its coins. This joint FinCEN/OFAC proposal would make that part of ongoing compliance programs: customer identification, suspicious-activity and currency-transaction reporting, sanctions screening, and the ability to block or freeze. Comments closed June 9, and there's no final rule yet. Some industry write-ups said freezes would reach tokens traded between holders, but the Act exempts direct person-to-person and self-custody transfers, so that claim isn't supported. Coin Center separately objected (Aug 21) to applying customer-ID rules to secondary-market transactions. Separately, on Nov 2 Tether, which issues the USDT stablecoin, said it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of an Oct 29 exchange hack that it said the FBI tied to North Korea. That was the company's own anti-theft step, not a government order, but it shows how fast an issuer can freeze coins.
2026-06963.why_it_matters: Freeze and seize capability built into the token itself becomes a legal condition of issuing the main regulated digital-dollar instrument. That gives authorities a built-in way to stop specific holders' funds on a court or agency order.
2026-06963.why_it_might_not: Freezes require a lawful order tied to specific coins or accounts, comparable to existing bank freezes under sanctions and court process, and major issuers already freeze voluntarily.

2026-21786.headline: Treasury proposes rules for the outbound investment law (COINS Act): a wider list of countries and technologies, with some deals banned and others requiring notice
2026-21786.org: U.S. Treasury, Office of Investment Security
2026-21786.what_changed: Treasury published a proposed rule (91 FR 67396; RIN 1505-AC94; docket TREAS-DO-2026-0595) to implement the COINS Act, which Congress passed in the FY2026 NDAA on Dec 18, 2025. It would create a new 31 CFR Part 851 to replace the Part 850 program that has applied since Jan 2, 2025.
2026-21786.summary: U.S. persons (citizens, green-card holders, U.S. entities and their foreign branches) would have to notify Treasury of some investments, and would be barred from others, in 'covered foreign persons' tied to countries of concern that work in listed technologies. Covered deals include buying equity or contingent equity, certain convertible or equity-like loans, joint ventures, greenfield projects, directing a foreign person's deal, and some limited-partner stakes in non-U.S. funds. U.S. parents would also answer for deals made by foreign subsidiaries they control. The countries of concern grow from China (including Hong Kong and Macau) to also cover Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela 'under the regime of Nicolas Maduro', which Treasury says no longer exists. The technologies grow from semiconductors, quantum and AI (renamed 'super intelligence systems') to add high-performance computing/supercomputing and hypersonics; Treasury's press release also lists biotechnology. The statute exempts bank lending, payment processing and clearing, underwriting, prime brokerage and global custody, plus de minimis deals at amounts Treasury has not yet set. National-interest exemptions are available.
2026-21786.why_it_matters: This is the only live federal framework that requires advance notice for, or outright bans, Americans' investments abroad. It now rests on a statute instead of an executive order, so it is more durable. The proposal widens the countries and sectors covered and lets Treasury add more technology categories through notice and comment. It also reaches indirect routes (fund-of-funds and LP stakes, structures that hide a U.S. person's role) and makes 'reasonable and diligent inquiry' a compliance duty.
2026-21786.why_it_might_not: It is targeted at national security. It covers only specified technology activities by entities linked to six named countries, and it does not limit ordinary payments, bank lending, custody or deposits. Treasury reports only about 100 notifications in roughly 21 months of the existing program. For most Americans it limits nothing about moving or holding money.

fdic-2026-22495.headline: FDIC proposal would move the largest banks under the 2008 'provisional hold' rule, for use if they fail

Holds apply only after a failure, while the FDIC separates insured from uninsured money. Some pass-through account holders, such as deposit brokers and agents, would have to be told they might not reach those deposits after a failure until they give the FDIC the required data.

genius-implementation-2026.what_changed: The OCC adopted its final GENIUS rule (new 12 CFR Part 15) on Oct 21, 2026, effective Jan 18, 2027. The Fed proposed reserve, capital and application rules on Sept 24, 2026, with comments due Nov 30. Treasury's section 3 proposal (2026-16796) closed for comment on Oct 19, 2026.
genius-implementation-2026.summary: From Jan 18, 2027, only licensed issuers may issue payment stablecoins in the U.S. Issuers must back coins fully with reserves such as short-term Treasury bills and meet redemption, capital and risk standards. Starting July 18, 2028, digital-asset service providers may not offer U.S. persons stablecoins from issuers that are not permitted. The OCC set BSA, AML and sanctions requirements aside for a separate rulemaking with Treasury. Treasury's proposal defines 'issue' to exclude transfers 'required by a lawful order'.
genius-implementation-2026.why_it_matters: This is building a regulated private digital-dollar system in which every compliant token carries freeze capability. It requires reserves in short-term Treasuries, which creates captive demand for government debt but only within the issuer sector.
genius-implementation-2026.why_it_might_not: It is licensing and prudential regulation of issuers. Holders face no new limits on withdrawing, redeeming or moving funds, and the rules include redemption standards.

hr1799-119.headline: House bill to raise cash and suspicious-activity reporting thresholds awaits a floor vote
hr1799-119.org: Rep. Loudermilk (sponsor); House Financial Services Committee
hr1799-119.what_changed: H.R. 1799, the Financial Reporting Threshold Modernization Act, was reported with an amendment on Mar 19, 2026 (H. Rept. 119-556; Union Calendar No. 478). No later floor action was confirmed.
hr1799-119.summary: As reported, the bill would raise the $10,000 cash-reporting threshold for non-financial businesses (31 U.S.C. 5331) to $30,000. It would also raise SAR thresholds from $5,000 to $10,000 and from $2,000 to $3,000, raise MSB-definition thresholds from $1,000 to $3,000, and index all of them to inflation every 5 years. It also directs a Treasury review of CTR and SAR requirements. This researcher did not verify the exact change to the bank CTR threshold under 31 U.S.C. 5313 in the reported text. A June 2026 House hearing, including Cato Institute testimony, also pushed to raise or repeal Bank Secrecy Act reporting thresholds.
hr1799-119.why_it_matters: It would roll back cash surveillance that has grown in real terms because the thresholds were never indexed. It also cuts against the GTO trend of lowering thresholds.
hr1799-119.why_it_might_not: It has not passed the House and has no Senate action, and it expires on Jan 3, 2027.

crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.headline: Hacks, hacking threats and outside-vendor failures lead crypto platforms outside the U.S. to pause withdrawals; South Korea's Gopax is still halted, and Brazil's Nubank paused for part of a day
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.org: Binance; Gopax (South Korea); Mercado Bitcoin, Nubank and Mercado Pago (Brazil)
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.who: Private cryptocurrency exchanges and fintech apps
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.what_changed: On Nov 6, Brazil's Nubank halted crypto deposits and withdrawals, and Mercado Pago blocked some crypto transfers to outside wallets, after problems at outside providers; Mercado Pago tied its problem to an incident at a risk-monitoring and anti-money-laundering vendor. Nubank restored deposits and withdrawals at 10 p.m. that night; Mercado Pago hadn't said by Nov 7 whether its transfers had resumed. South Korea's Gopax, which halted withdrawals, trading and deposits on Nov 6 after hacking threats, still had no date to reopen on Nov 8 and was handling withdrawals only by manual review; a senior Korean financial regulator said Gopax is believed to have received about two threatening emails and appears to have reported to authorities before suspending service, and the Financial Supervisory Service plans to meet exchange and custody firms' security chiefs on Nov 19. Binance, hacked for about $6.3 billion on Oct 29, has kept reopening withdrawals in phases since Nov 1, and Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin halted withdrawals Nov 2 after about $40 million was drained.
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.summary: These were company decisions after thefts, threats or vendor failures, not government limits on customers' money. Binance said it would cover losses, and Binance is Gopax's majority shareholder. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze wallets holding stolen coins, about $3 billion in total, which shows the freeze ability that U.S. rules will require issuers to have for lawful orders. The Brazil pauses show that a failure at an outside data or compliance vendor can stop transfers even when the platform itself isn't hacked. Binance.US, a separate U.S. platform, said it was not affected by the hack.
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.why_it_matters: Withdrawal pauses at big platforms can spread fear and claims that capital controls are starting. The stablecoin freezes show how quickly issuers can block coins, an ability U.S. rules will soon require, and the Brazil cases show how one outside compliance vendor can halt transfers at several firms.
crypto-exchange-withdrawal-pauses-2026-1.why_it_might_not: The pauses were company security or technical steps at platforms outside the U.S., not government orders to limit customers' money; Nubank reopened the same night and Binance has been reopening in phases.

2026-22809.headline: FinCEN and the Fed drop a 2020 plan to cut the record-keeping threshold for transfers abroad from $3,000 to $250
2026-22809.org: FinCEN (Treasury) and the Federal Reserve Board
2026-22809.what_changed: FinCEN and the Fed announced on Nov 6, 2026, that they were withdrawing their October 2020 joint proposal (85 FR 68005; RIN 1506-AB41). The withdrawal notice (FR Doc 2026-22809) was published in the Federal Register on Nov 9, making the withdrawal official.
2026-22809.summary: The 2020 proposal would have lowered, from $3,000 to $250, the amount at which banks and money transmitters must collect and keep sender and recipient details on funds transfers that begin or end outside the U.S., and the amount at which FinCEN's travel rule requires passing those details along the payment chain. It also would have stated that these rules cover crypto and digital assets with legal-tender status. The agencies said they received nearly 3,000 comments, mostly opposed; that more than five years had passed; and that crypto markets and laws, including the GENIUS Act, have changed. They said no similar final rule will be issued without a new chance for public comment. The $3,000 threshold stays in place.
2026-22809.why_it_matters: It retires a long-pending plan that would have brought far more everyday transfers abroad, such as family remittances, under record-keeping and pass-along requirements, and the agencies committed to new public comment before trying anything similar.
2026-22809.why_it_might_not: The existing $3,000 rules stay in place, and the agencies left room for future changes aimed at crypto. Tighter reporting can still come through other tools, such as geographic targeting orders like the Minnesota and Southwest border orders, or rules to carry out FATF's new payment-transparency standard.

Treasury says MEXC Global, one of the 20 largest crypto exchanges in the world, facilitated at least $16 billion in transactions tied to Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion and to cybercrime between May 2021 and May 2026. The order covers MEXC's subsidiaries, branches, offices and successors outside the U.S., and it explains how covered institutions should handle crypto that arrives from MEXC when it can't be rejected. It doesn't change existing reporting or sanctions duties and has no end date. MEXC said its operations were normal and that it had started an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls. The order names one foreign company; it doesn't limit transfers to other platforms or ordinary transfers abroad.
fincen-9714-mexc-global.why_it_matters: It's a direct ban on a channel for moving money, imposed with an anti-money-laundering power rather than ordinary sanctions, against one of the world's larger crypto exchanges. It shows how quickly U.S. institutions can be cut off from a named platform.

Both came out before the first report; added Nov 7 for context, not as new movement.
intl-imf-stablecoin-flows-capital-contro.summary: The working paper estimates $21.4 trillion in gross international stablecoin flows from 2018 to 2025, with emerging and developing economies holding three quarters of stablecoins. It finds stablecoin activity rises about 30% in the six months after a country restricts capital outflows and doesn't fall back when the restrictions end, and that holdings rise about 75% within a year of a currency crisis. The departmental paper says stablecoins issued mostly in U.S. dollars by a few jurisdictions could reshape capital flows and currency substitution in other countries, and it outlines possible responses on macro-financial policy, regulation, data collection and international cooperation. intl-imf-stablecoin-flows-capital-contro.why_it_might_not: It's research and early policy thinking about other countries, not a recommendation to limit Americans, and the U.S. already regulates its own dollar stablecoins under the GENIUS Act.

Alternative assets include private equity and debt, real estate, commodities, infrastructure, lifetime-income strategies and actively managed funds that hold digital assets. The rule carries out an August 2025 executive order (EO 14330). dol-1210-AC38-401k-alternatives.why_it_might_not: It's a legal safe harbor, not a mandate: employers still decide what their plans offer, the final text could change, and the proposal doesn't address withdrawals or rollovers. foster-real-time-regulatory-study-act-dr.summary: A one-page summary lists modules such as regulatory dashboards, automated bank and credit union reports, stress tests on historical and current data, AI risk monitoring, and automated fraud and anti-money-laundering screening. Foster's release says AI and round-the-clock payment systems could spread financial stress quickly, and that real-time tools could help regulators respond faster and prepare for orderly bank resolutions. It is a draft, not an introduced bill.
foster-real-time-regulatory-study-act-dr.why_it_matters: Real-time data would give regulators a faster view of trouble at banks, such as sudden deposit outflows, and shape how quickly they could respond to a run. Its author is likely to gain influence when his party takes control of Congress.

intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.org: Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission and National Financial Stabilization Fund; South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.what_changed: On Nov 9, the steps announced Nov 6 took effect: Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission cut intraday short sales of borrowed shares to 3% of a stock's average daily volume over the prior 30 trading days (from 30%) and raised the minimum short-sale margin from 90% to 130%, and South Korea exempted brokerages from the 140% minimum collateral ratio on margin loans through Jan 31. Asian markets were mixed that day: MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 0.8% by midday after falling 4.6% the week before, while South Korea's KOSPI closed 0.8% lower. On Nov 6, Japan's Nikkei had fallen 5.96%, South Korea's KOSPI 6.02% and Taiwan's index 4.5%, Korea's exchange paused trading for 20 minutes under its automatic circuit breaker, and Taiwan's National Financial Stabilization Fund authorized buying stocks, its 10th activation.
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.summary: The selloff followed the Nov 3 U.S. midterm elections and worries that the results would slow AI and data center spending. The steps aim to support prices: buying stocks, curbing bets on falling prices, and easing margin calls so fewer investors are forced to sell. Several people told Reuters that Taiwan's Finance Ministry asked state-owned banks to support the market. Taiwan's fund cited record foreign selling of NT$994 billion in October and NT$524 billion more in November through Nov 6. None of these steps limits bank withdrawals, currency exchange or moving money abroad. On Nov 12, Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission said it has set no end date for the short-selling limits and reviews them daily; short sales of borrowed shares fell to 1.7% to 2% of main-board turnover on Nov 9-11, from 2.97% on Nov 6. Taiwan's main index fell 2.63% on Nov 12.
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.why_it_matters: It shows how quickly governments step into markets during a sharp selloff, including limits on one kind of trade. Steps like these can fuel claims that broader limits on selling or moving money are next.
intl-asia-market-support-2026-11-06.why_it_might_not: State stock-buying funds and short-sale curbs are familiar, temporary tools in Asian markets. They don't stop investors from selling shares they own or from moving their money, and the U.S. has no similar state stock fund.

japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.org: Shinkin Central Bank and Shinkin Kyodo Center (Japan)
japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.what_changed: Around 1:30 p.m. on Nov 6, a failure in the shared network system for shinkin banks left customers of 128 institutions, mainly in western Japan, unable to use ATMs or make deposits and withdrawals at branch counters; online banking was also reported down. Shinkin Central Bank and the Shinkin Kyodo Center said service was fully restored shortly after 7 p.m. the same day and that the cause was an equipment malfunction, not a cyberattack.
japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.summary: Shinkin banks are community lenders that share a central computer system; the outage hit the network's western center, while banks in eastern Japan worked normally. Some outlets called it a banking crisis, but it was a technical failure lasting about six hours, not a government action or a bank run. It has no link to U.S. banks.
japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.why_it_matters: Outages that stop people from getting cash, even briefly, can spark rumors of frozen accounts, so it helps to know when a halt is technical.
japan-shinkin-outage-2026-11-06.why_it_might_not: It was a hardware fault fixed the same evening, at small regional banks in another country, with no government order involved.

paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.headline: Paraguay's central bank plans to move failed Ueno Bank's accounts to several banks in lots after finding about $600 million in sound assets; covered savers have received advances of up to about $19,000
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.org: Banco Central del Paraguay (Paraguay's central bank) and its banking and securities supervisors
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.what_changed: On Nov 12, 2026, central bank president Jorge Schreiner said auditors had preliminarily found about $600 million in sound assets at Ueno, more than the bank owes to pension funds such as the Social Security Institute (IPS), whose deposits and investments there total about $516 million. After a review of 8 to 10 days to draw up an 'exclusion balance' of sound assets against liabilities, the central bank plans to tender Ueno's assets and deposits in lots to several local banks, so no single bank takes on more than it can handle, with the Deposit Guarantee Fund able to cover any gap. If accounts move before pending payouts are made, their holders would become customers of the receiving bank instead of being paid out. Pension funds have legal priority. This follows the Nov 11 completion of advances of up to 40 monthly minimum wages (about $19,000) to all 1,812,348 savers the fund covers.
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.summary: Paraguay's central bank put Ueno, a digital lender that said it had about 3 million customers, into resolution (a state-run wind-down) on Nov 3 after its solvency ratio fell below half the legal minimum, freezing accounts except for guarantee-fund payouts. AFP reported that Ueno held about $2.8 billion when it was taken over, so the advances cover only part of the money at the bank. The fund's limit is 75 monthly minimum wages (about $37,000) per depositor; EFE reported that payments up to that limit are to be extended from the week of Nov 16, and officials haven't said what happens to balances above it. The guarantee excludes the bank's directors and shareholders, and investors in Ueno's money funds, which aren't bank deposits, are still waiting for a decision on their money. Paraguay's Senate removed President Santiago Peña on Nov 6 over his links to the bank, and prosecutors are investigating.
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.why_it_matters: It shows in real time what a large bank failure can mean for savers: accounts frozen, covered money returned in stages over about a week, and larger balances and investment funds tied to the bank left waiting. That is the kind of situation U.S. failed-bank rules, such as the FDIC's pending 'provisional hold' proposal for the largest banks, are designed to handle.
paraguay-ueno-bank-resolution-2026-11.why_it_might_not: It is one failed bank in another country, handled under Paraguay's own deposit-guarantee law, and every covered saver has received an advance. In the U.S., deposits are insured up to at least $250,000 per depositor at each FDIC-insured bank, and the FDIC's list shows no U.S. bank failures since Sept 25.

next_milestone.what: Central bank review of Ueno's sound assets and debts, expected to take 8 to 10 days from Nov 12, then a tender moving its assets and deposits to several banks in lots; Paraguay's state pension fund pays the 32,000 pensioners who banked at Ueno through other banks on Nov 17

intl-china-market-support-2026-11.headline: China pauses new stock listings and large share sales by big shareholders, and makes stock-market stability a top task after a tech-stock slide
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.org: China Securities Regulatory Commission and the State Council (China's cabinet)
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.what_changed: On Nov 6, a State Council executive meeting chaired by Premier Li Qiang called for improving the system for stabilizing the capital market and strengthening the stock market's stability; Chinese media reported on Nov 9 that it was the first time the phrase had appeared at such a meeting. Earlier, on Nov 3, the Financial Times reported, and Reuters relayed, that the China Securities Regulatory Commission had given investment banks informal 'window guidance' to pause initial public offerings and had suspended large share sales by existing shareholders until markets recover; Reuters said it couldn't verify the report. On Nov 2, the securities regulator eased its rules on company share buybacks, and the central bank made a lending program that funds buybacks long-term.
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.summary: China's blue-chip CSI 300 index fell 8.5% in October, its worst month in more than a decade, and the STAR 50 index of tech shares is about 40% below its July peak. Because the pauses were given as informal guidance rather than published rules, their exact scope and end date aren't public. China already limits how much money its people can move abroad, including a $50,000 yearly cap on individuals' U.S. dollar purchases. The reported steps restrict new share supply and selling by big holders; we found no reports of limits on ordinary investors selling shares or withdrawing bank deposits.
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.why_it_matters: It's a live example of a government limiting who can sell shares during a market slide, close to the limits on selling financial assets this monitor watches for. It came days after Taiwan and South Korea took their own market-support steps.
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.why_it_might_not: It's in China, which already tightly controls money leaving the country, and it targets new listings and large sales by big shareholders, not ordinary investors or bank deposits. It was given as informal guidance, and its scope hasn't been published.
intl-china-market-support-2026-11.us_link: No direct link. We found no U.S. step to pause listings or limit share sales; U.S. exchanges rely on automatic, marketwide circuit breakers.

intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.headline: Lebanon's central bank raises monthly withdrawal limits on dollar deposits frozen since 2019 to $1,200 and $600, from Dec 1
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.what_changed: On Nov 3, 2026, Banque du Liban issued Intermediate Circulars 780 and 781, raising the monthly amounts eligible depositors can draw from dollar accounts frozen since the 2019 crisis: to $1,200 from $1,000 under Basic Circular 158, and to $600 from $500 under Basic Circular 166. The cash portions stay at $800 and $400; the increases apply only to card payments at points of sale, now $400 and $200. The changes take effect Dec 1, 2026 and run until June 30, 2027 unless modified or renewed.
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.summary: Lebanese banks have limited depositors' access to their dollar savings since the 2019 financial collapse, and these circulars are the main way depositors get some money back while Parliament has yet to pass a law on repaying deposits. The central bank cited the exceptional circumstances Lebanon faces, including weak economic activity and rising prices, and said amounts paid will be deducted from any future repayment under that law. It said the card-only increase aims to preserve resources, encourage secure and traceable transactions and promote non-cash payments. According to a Lebanese news analysis, the circulars have cost the central bank about $6.1 billion since they began, and the increase raises its monthly outlay from about $240 million to $300 million.
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.why_it_matters: Lebanon is one of the clearest modern examples of long-lasting limits on bank withdrawals: years later, savers can still take out only small monthly amounts. The new room is steered to card spending, which keeps more transactions traceable and inside the banking system.
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.why_it_might_not: It loosens existing limits rather than adding new ones, and it stems from Lebanon's own 2019 banking collapse and frozen dollar deposits, conditions that don't exist in the U.S.
intl-lebanon-withdrawal-limits-2026-11.us_link: No direct link. U.S. deposits are insured up to $250,000 per depositor at each insured bank, and no U.S. withdrawal limits are in place or proposed.

us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.org: SoFi Bank, N.A. (a national bank supervised by the OCC)
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.who: SoFi Technologies, a digital financial services company whose bank subsidiary is nationally chartered; it reports 15.8 million members
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.what_changed: On Oct 22, 2026, SoFi launched SoFi Earn (SOFIE), which it calls the first and only national bank-issued tokenized deposit for consumers. Each SOFIE represents $1 held on deposit at SoFi Bank, earns interest (4.40% APY as of Oct 20) and is FDIC-insured up to the usual limits. Members can convert it 1:1 to SoFiUSD, the bank's stablecoin, to buy crypto or send money to outside wallets over blockchain networks 24/7. SoFi said the product is rolling out to its crypto customers through November.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.summary: A tokenized deposit is an ordinary bank deposit recorded as a digital token on a blockchain. SoFi says SOFIE is a deposit, not a payment stablecoin; SoFiUSD, launched in December 2025, is what SoFi calls the first stablecoin issued by a U.S. national bank. The announcement doesn't describe any spending conditions or programmable rules on customers' money. It is an optional product from one bank and wasn't covered in earlier reports.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.official_acknowledgment: Company announcement; no regulator statement on SOFIE found.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.linked_bills_or_rules: GENIUS Act stablecoin rules (relevant to SoFiUSD); related to the tracked tokenized-deposit projects at Wells Fargo and The Clearing House.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.why_it_matters: It brings bank-issued digital tokens to ordinary consumers, not just businesses, as stablecoin rules take shape. Money on blockchain rails can move around the clock and leaves a lasting record of transfers, and payment stablecoins like SoFiUSD will fall under GENIUS Act rules that require issuers to be able to freeze coins on lawful orders.
us-sofi-consumer-tokenized-deposit.why_it_might_not: It's an optional product from one bank, insured like other deposits, and the announcement describes no spending conditions or limits set by the bank or the government. It doesn't change how ordinary bank accounts work.

intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.headline: Bolivia speeds up the return of dollar savings that have been hard to withdraw since 2023 and lets banks keep new dollar deposits on hand
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.org: Banco Central de Bolivia (Bolivia's central bank)
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.what_changed: Under board Resolution 157/2026, announced Oct 30, 2026, Bolivia's central bank moved up to Nov 5 the repayment of $333 million to households with dollar deposits of $10,001 to $50,000, payments that had been scheduled between Nov 16, 2026 and Mar 16, 2027. From Nov 9, banks and other lenders manage the required reserves on new dollar deposits themselves, so those dollars stay available to pay depositors' withdrawals. The central bank also cut the share of local-currency funds that non-bank lenders must keep in its custody from 80% to 60%.
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.summary: A shortage of U.S. dollars has made it hard for Bolivians to withdraw their dollar deposits since February 2023, a freeze on access to savings that the central bank itself calls a 'corralito.' In May 2026 the authorities set a schedule to return dollar deposits in stages by balance size, and withdrawals are voluntary; after this change, the remaining stages for individuals, covering balances above $50,000, run from April to July 2027, and companies follow a separate schedule through December 2028. The central bank says it and the banks mobilized more than $300 million to pay early, and that the reserve change aims to avoid repeating the freeze for new dollar savings. A Bolivian newspaper reported that some customers still had trouble depositing cash dollars, and a former economy minister said dollar transfers and payments remain restricted, with fees of 7% to 10% on some operations.
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.why_it_matters: Bolivia is a current example of how a dollar shortage can turn into years of limits on getting money out of the bank, and of how slowly such limits unwind: savers are being repaid in stages over more than a year.
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.why_it_might_not: This loosens existing limits rather than adding new ones, and it stems from Bolivia's own shortage of U.S. dollars. The U.S. issues dollars and faces no such shortage, and no U.S. withdrawal limits are in place or proposed.
intl-bolivia-dollar-deposit-refunds-2026.us_link: No direct link. U.S. deposits are insured up to $250,000 per depositor at each insured bank, and no U.S. withdrawal limits are in place or proposed.

intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.headline: Canada's government proposes barring most businesses from accepting $10,000 or more in cash and capping crypto ATM use at $1,000 a day
intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.org: Government of Canada (Department of Finance), Senate Bill S-8
intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.what_changed: On Nov 3, 2026, Canada's government introduced Bill S-8, the Combatting Financial Crimes and Drug Trafficking Act, in the Senate, where it awaits second reading. It would bar certain businesses and other entities from accepting cash payments, donations or deposits of $10,000 or more, and bar many financial firms from accepting cash deposits into an account from someone who isn't the account holder or authorized on it. It would also make it a crime to run a crypto ATM without a provincial or territorial license and require licensed machines to keep each user's transactions to no more than $1,000 in any 24 hours.
intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.summary: Canada's Finance Department says cash remains a preferred payment method for criminals and that Canada and Japan are the only G7 countries without a framework to restrict or regulate large cash transactions across the economy. Under the bill, the cash limit would cover one payment or a series of related payments; banks and credit unions are exempt so cash can still be deposited, and cheques, cards and electronic transfers aren't limited. The bill would also let the Finance Minister temporarily suspend registrations of money services businesses (such as money transfer and currency exchange firms), direct Canada's financial intelligence agency to refuse or revoke them, and make regulations to temporarily limit or prohibit certain domestic transactions in prescribed circumstances; the government says these tools can already be used for transactions to or from foreign countries. Crypto ATM rules would start 90 to 180 days after the bill becomes law and the ban on unlicensed machines after 18 months. Similar cash limits were first proposed in a 2025 bill. The bill still has to pass the Senate and the House of Commons.

intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.why_it_matters: It goes beyond reporting: a close U.S. neighbor and G7 member would ban many large cash payments outright and give its finance minister power to limit some domestic transactions. Canada's government says most G7 countries already restrict large cash transactions, so the idea is common among U.S. allies.
intl-canada-bill-s8-cash-limits.why_it_might_not: It's a bill at the first stage in Canada, aimed at fraud, drug money and money laundering. Bank and credit union deposits are exempt, and cards, cheques and electronic transfers aren't limited. In the U.S., businesses must report cash payments over $10,000 but may accept them, and we found no U.S. proposal to cap them.

intl-fsb-turkiye-stablecoin-review-2026-.headline: Global regulators' review urges Türkiye to set up a stablecoin regime, citing risks of digital dollarization and sudden capital outflows
intl-fsb-turkiye-stablecoin-review-2026-.org: Financial Stability Board (FSB), the group of financial regulators that reports to the G20
intl-fsb-turkiye-stablecoin-review-2026-.what_changed: On Nov 11, 2026, the FSB published its second peer review of Türkiye, which examined the country's rules for crypto-assets and stablecoins. It recommends that Türkiye set up a financial stability monitoring framework with specific indicators for risk channels such as cross-border capital flows, establish a dedicated regime for stablecoins, strengthen supervision and enforcement, including against offshore platforms that reach Turkish users, and improve cross-border cooperation and information sharing.
intl-fsb-turkiye-stablecoin-review-2026-.summary: The review says Türkiye has brought much of its crypto market under registration and licensing and already prohibits using crypto-assets for domestic payments, but has no framework for regulating stablecoin issuers. It reports that Türkiye's central bank and banking regulator see foreign-issued stablecoins and offshore platforms as able to amplify swings in capital flows, deepen digital dollarization (people swapping their own currency for digital dollars) and raise the risk of sudden capital outflows, though the authorities called these channels limited for now. The FSB adds that in emerging economies, crypto risks can interact with how well capital flow measures work. Türkiye volunteered for the review, and FSB recommendations aren't binding.

intl-fsb-turkiye-stablecoin-review-2026-.why_it_matters: It's another sign that international bodies see dollar stablecoins as a way around countries' limits on moving money, and that their answer is more monitoring and rules for stablecoins and the platforms that offer them, the same theme as the IMF research this monitor tracks.
intl-fsb-turkiye-stablecoin-review-2026-.why_it_might_not: It's a non-binding review of one country's crypto rules, and it doesn't recommend capital controls. Nothing in it applies to the U.S. or limits Americans' transfers.

intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.headline: South Korea's financial regulator will let crypto exchanges block deposits and withdrawals when a hack is suspected
intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.what_changed: On Nov 12, 2026, the FSC said it will issue a no-action letter, a written promise not to penalize, so crypto exchanges can block deposits and withdrawals under certain conditions when a hack or breach is suspected. Current law lets them block only when a hack has clearly happened. Emergency guidelines that apply right away require round-the-clock monitoring; exchanges that can't monitor at all hours must process deposits and withdrawals only during hours when their systems run normally, and tell users in advance.
intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.summary: The FSC pointed to the $6.3 billion Binance hack as showing that fast blocking limits harm to users; its release doesn't mention Gopax, which halted withdrawals on Nov 6 after hacking threats (tracked under How banks are doing). The FSC also told exchanges to keep as little of users' crypto online as possible and to carry more insurance and reserves, and said a government Digital Asset Act bill due soon would give crypto firms security standards and liability like financial firms'. FSC Vice Chairman Shin Jin-chang said domestic exchanges hold about 66 trillion won of crypto for more than 10 million users. The letter hadn't been issued as of Nov 12, and the FSC didn't spell out the conditions.
intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.plain: South Korea will let crypto (digital coin) exchanges stop withdrawals if they suspect a hack. Some exchanges may only handle withdrawals during staffed hours. This is in South Korea, not the U.S.
intl-korea-crypto-withdrawal-blocks-2026.why_it_matters: A government is widening when people can be stopped from taking money out of a platform, even before a hack is confirmed, and limiting some exchanges' withdrawals to staffed hours. It shows how security rules can add new pauses on access to money.

intl-russia-retail-crypto-caps-2026-11.headline: Russia lets ordinary investors buy bitcoin, ether and USDT from Nov 17, capped at 300,000 rubles a year per firm
intl-russia-retail-crypto-caps-2026-11.what_changed: A Bank of Russia ordinance published Nov 6, 2026 and taking effect Nov 17 lists bitcoin, ether and the dollar stablecoin USDT as the crypto assets that non-qualified (ordinary) investors may buy, through brokers, trust managers or crypto exchange offices, on exchanges or over the counter. Purchases through any one intermediary may not exceed 300,000 rubles (about $3,700) a year. Qualified investors face no limit, and every investor must first pass a test and read about the risks.
intl-russia-retail-crypto-caps-2026-11.summary: The rules build on a law signed Aug 4, 2026 that set up a regulated crypto market under central bank oversight. Reports say separate exchange trading rules take effect Nov 22, and Moscow Exchange plans to start crypto trading Dec 1. Cointelegraph, citing the Bank of Russia, reported that transfers from regulated accounts to personal (self-custody) wallets are already banned, that peer-to-peer crypto trading will be banned from July 1, 2027, and that paying for goods with crypto remains banned. Russia also runs a digital ruble with a monthly top-up cap (tracked).
intl-russia-retail-crypto-caps-2026-11.plain: From Nov 17, people in Russia can buy bitcoin and two other digital coins from licensed firms. Buyers who are not pros can spend up to 300,000 rubles (about $3,700) a year at each firm.
intl-russia-retail-crypto-caps-2026-11.why_it_matters: It's a live example of a government capping how much ordinary people can put into crypto, including a dollar-linked coin, and keeping those coins inside licensed, monitored accounts.
intl-russia-retail-crypto-caps-2026-11.why_it_might_not: It mainly opens a legal route for Russians to buy crypto, and qualified investors face no cap. It doesn't affect Americans.
intl-russia-retail-crypto-caps-2026-11.us_link: No direct link. U.S. rules set no cap on how much crypto Americans may buy, and FinCEN withdrew its proposed reporting rule for transfers to personal crypto wallets on Oct 5, 2026 (tracked).

tether-tron-chainalysis-dctf-2026-11.headline: Tether, TRON and Chainalysis launch a private task force to find illicit USDT and get it frozen before it moves
tether-tron-chainalysis-dctf-2026-11.who: Tether, which issues the USDT stablecoin; TRON, the blockchain network founded by Justin Sun; and Chainalysis, a blockchain-intelligence firm
tether-tron-chainalysis-dctf-2026-11.what_changed: On Nov 12, 2026, the three companies announced the Digital Crime Task Force. It will search for suspected scams, hacks, laundering and other crime involving Tether's USDT on the TRON blockchain, turn what it finds into leads for police, and coordinate with law enforcement on investigations and asset freezes before criminals can move the money. It will also take tips and freeze requests from police.
tether-tron-chainalysis-dctf-2026-11.summary: Tether says it has frozen more than $7 billion linked to illicit activity, working with more than 360 law enforcement agencies in 73 countries. Chainalysis supplies investigators, blockchain data and AI tools. The group follows the T3 Financial Crime Unit that Tether and TRON set up with TRM Labs in 2024, which Bloomberg reported disbanded in late August. The announcement gives no deadlines or results yet. It is a private effort, not a government rule, and it covers only USDT on TRON.
tether-tron-chainalysis-dctf-2026-11.plain: Tether, a company that makes a digital coin tied to the dollar, started a task force with two tech firms. It will look for stolen or criminal coins and work with police to freeze them quickly.

quote.text: waiting for a victim to report a crime is no longer good enough

tether-tron-chainalysis-dctf-2026-11.official_acknowledgment: Company announcement; it says the group will coordinate with law enforcement and take freeze requests from police. We found no government statement on the task force.
tether-tron-chainalysis-dctf-2026-11.linked_bills_or_rules: GENIUS Act rules that will require payment stablecoin issuers to be able to freeze coins on lawful orders (tracked: the FinCEN/OFAC proposal and the GENIUS Act effective date, Jan 18, 2027).
tether-tron-chainalysis-dctf-2026-11.why_it_matters: It shifts stablecoin freezes from reacting to reported crimes toward actively hunting for suspect funds, which widens how often and how fast a company can stop dollar-linked coins from moving. U.S. rules will soon require payment stablecoin issuers to be able to freeze coins on lawful orders.
tether-tron-chainalysis-dctf-2026-11.why_it_might_not: It's a private effort aimed at scams, hacks and other crime, and freezes are coordinated with police. It covers only USDT on one blockchain, and it doesn't touch bank accounts, cash or other ways to pay.

tx-crypto-atm-ban-bills-90r.headline: Texas bills would ban crypto ATMs in the state
tx-crypto-atm-ban-bills-90r.org: Texas Legislature (Sen. Hagenbuch; Reps. Shofner and Little)
tx-crypto-atm-ban-bills-90r.what_changed: Three bills prefiled for Texas's 2027 session would ban operating virtual currency kiosks, machines that exchange crypto for money or bank credit: SB 181 (filed Nov 9) with a civil penalty equal to the kiosk's revenue, HB 271 (filed Nov 9) as a criminal offense, and HB 1082 (filed Nov 12) as a state jail felony. Each would take effect Sept 1, 2027 if passed.
tx-crypto-atm-ban-bills-90r.summary: The bills define a kiosk as an electronic terminal that exchanges virtual currency for money, bank credit or other virtual currency; SB 181 and HB 1082 would also cover people who let a kiosk operate on property they own or control. The bill texts don't state a reason. They don't limit bank accounts, cash withdrawals or buying crypto through other platforms. Canada's Bill S-8 (tracked) would instead license the machines and cap use at $1,000 a day.
tx-crypto-atm-ban-bills-90r.plain: Three Texas bills would ban crypto ATMs, machines that swap cash for digital coins. They would not limit bank accounts or cash. They are early bills that have had no votes.
tx-crypto-atm-ban-bills-90r.why_it_matters: It would close one way for Texans to turn cash into crypto, going further than Canada's proposed daily cap. Lawmakers in both chambers filed versions, so the idea has more than one backer.
tx-crypto-atm-ban-bills-90r.why_it_might_not: These are prefiled state bills that haven't had hearings. They target one kind of machine and leave bank accounts, cash and other ways to buy crypto untouched.

next_milestone.what: Texas Legislature convenes; the bills can then be referred to committees

tx-hb165-90r.headline: Texas bill would require, not just allow, a state payment system that uses gold- and silver-backed currency
tx-hb165-90r.what_changed: Filed Nov 9, 2026 for the 2027 session, HB 165 would amend the 2025 law that lets the state comptroller set up or authorize electronic systems for paying with a currency backed by gold and silver bullion held in the Texas Bullion Depository, starting May 1, 2027. The bill changes 'may' to 'shall,' so the comptroller would have to set up or authorize such a system. If passed, it would take effect Sept 1, 2027.
tx-hb165-90r.summary: The 2025 law (HB 1056) also recognized gold and silver coin as legal tender in Texas from Sept 1, 2026, without requiring anyone to offer or accept it. HB 165 was filed on Nov 9, the first day of bill filing for the 2027 session; the Legislature convenes Jan 12, 2027, and the bill would need committee and floor votes in both chambers.
tx-hb165-90r.plain: A Texas lawmaker filed a bill that would make the state set up a way to pay with gold- and silver-backed money. Current law allows this but does not require it.
tx-hb165-90r.why_it_matters: It would guarantee Texans a state-run way to pay with gold- and silver-backed money, an alternative to bank deposits that works against any future limit on holding or using gold.
tx-hb165-90r.why_it_might_not: It's a prefiled bill that hasn't had a hearing, and current law already allows the system. Payments would run through the state depository, and federal tax rules on gold don't change.

next_milestone.what: Texas Legislature convenes; the bill can then be referred to a committee
